push.title: Notifications on this device
push.hint: Madar sends one short line when you have a new notice or message: who sent it and the first words. A person who sees your locked phone can read it.
push.ask: Get one short line on this device when you have a new notice or message.
push.unsupported: This browser cannot show Madar notifications. Use a recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
push.needsInstall: To get notifications on an iPhone, add Madar to the Home Screen first. Then open Madar from the Home Screen, go to Settings and turn on “Notify me on this device”.
push.blocked: This browser blocks notifications from Madar. Allow notifications for this site in the browser settings. Then open Settings again and turn on “Notify me on this device”.
push.notSet: Notifications are not set up on this copy of Madar yet.
push.error: Madar could not turn on notifications on this device. Try again.
push.offError: Madar could not turn off notifications on this device. Try again.
push.notificationBody: You have something new in Madar.
push.homeScreenLine: On an iPhone or iPad, Madar can send notifications only from the Home Screen. Add it there in 3 steps:
push.homeScreenStep1: Tap Share in your browser. In Safari, it can be under •••.
push.homeScreenStep3: Open Madar from its new icon, sign in, and tap “Turn on notifications”.
push.installLine: Add Madar to your Home Screen. It then opens like an app, in its own window.

2026-10-23-71.title: Notifications say who and what
2026-10-23-71.body: A notification now shows who wrote and the first words, as in WhatsApp. A notice shows the same sentence as the bell. Tap it, and Madar opens that chat or task. Open Madar once on each phone, so it can start.

2026-10-23-70.title: Notifications on your phone
2026-10-23-70.body: On an iPhone, Home now shows 3 steps that add Madar to the Home Screen. An iPhone gets notifications only from there. On Android, Home shows one button that adds Madar to the Home Screen. Notifications now reach a phone in sleep mode at once. They also reach a phone that had no signal for some hours.
